DPJ9-Checkout-Judgment-Packs/solution/DE.content:
# Reference decision record
## Observed pressure
Legacy quote and receipt duplicate membership price and shipping decisions. A threshold change risks updating only one endpoint.

## Chosen change and simpler counterfactual
Keep the existing domain records and static API. Centralize price/shipping in quote's two helpers; have receipt render quote's Totals. For this fixed rule set, these ordinary methods are sufficient. A service container and policy hierarchy add wiring without an independent runtime variation requirement.

## Measurement and rollback
The two legacy entrypoints each contain a pricing/delivery decision set; target quote has one centralized set and receipt reuses it. No new domain/interface class is added for core. All606valid combinations are checked for both legacy and target, with exact receipt output and invalid-call cases. A source diff establishes structure; passing outputs establish behavior within the bounded contract. Commit the baseline, extract one helper or redirect one endpoint at a time, run checks after each change, and retain that baseline as the rollback target. A performance improvement is not claimed.

## Optional variation
A requested per-call partner shipping rule creates a real selection seam. quoteWith injects one function without changing quote. It could earn named policy classes if policies later need independent state, configuration or lifecycle. Remove the injection when that independent variation disappears.

DPJ9-Checkout-Judgment-Packs/solution/RE.content:
# Checkout refactoring judgment
Use Java 21. Preserve LegacyCheckout, Order, Totals and ContractTests as the behavioral baseline.
The program uses only bounded integers, reads no input and writes no files.

```sh
javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror -d classes @sources.txt
java -cp classes ContractTests base
java -cp classes Main base
java -cp classes ContractTests core
java -cp classes Main
```
Baseline runs before either core method is complete. The untouched starter compiles and explicitly rejects its first unfinished quote. Complete Checkout.quote and receipt, preserving the public behavior. The reference centralizes stable rules in ordinary helper methods; a larger pattern hierarchy requires a concrete change pressure and cost argument. The helper skeleton supplies one possible route rather than a requirement to preserve that internal structure.

Order has 0..100 units, REGULAR/MEMBER tier and PICKUP/STANDARD/EXPRESS delivery, all non-null. Prices are integer cents: regular 200/unit, member 180/unit. Zero units and pickup have zero shipping. Positive-unit express always costs 900. Standard costs 500 unless subtotal >= 2000, when it is free. Membership affects subtotal, so it can change eligibility for free standard delivery. Totals are immutable nonnegative values; total uses checked int addition. Receipt is the exact six-field pipe-separated tier|delivery|units|subtotal|shipping|total string. Missing order is rejected with NullPointerException.

Main without arguments prints:
```text
REGULAR|STANDARD|10|2000|0|2000
REGULAR|STANDARD|10|2000|0|2000
2700
```
Main base prints the first receipt and 2700. Both legacy entrypoints are checked against an independently written rule table over all 606 allowed combinations. Core also checks both target entrypoints. Behavioral tests do not prove design quality, removal of duplication or a justified pattern choice. Keep your decision and measurements in DECISIONS.md.

Optional quoteWith receives one trusted ToIntFunction<Order> shipping policy, called exactly once, even for zero units. It replaces the normal shipping calculation for this call only. Return 0..10000 cents; null input/policy, invalid fee and callback exceptions fail. Baseline quote behavior stays unchanged. This extension has an actual variation seam; an injected function is enough before separate policy classes earn their cost. Run the full ContractTests after core to verify it.

# Decision record
Record the concrete duplication/change pressure, observable contract, chosen design and simpler alternative.
Measure rule locations and added types/indirection before/after. Keep the definition of each count.
Record one behavior-preserving step per commit, matching checks and a rollback target.
For optional policy injection, explain the actual variation and a removal trigger.

DPJ9-Judgment-Worked-Example/README.md.content:
# Smaller refactor or selected behavior
Java 21:
```sh
javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror Main.java ContractTests.java
java ContractTests
java Main
```
Main prints NOTICE: HELLO three times, once per implementation.

Legacy duplicates the format rule in banner and email. Direct centralizes that fixed rule
and retains both entrypoints. Pluggable receives a function, introducing a field and constructor
and moving behavior selection to composition. It earns that flexibility only when independently
selected behavior is needed. The main outputs stay equal; a custom injected rule deliberately
has a different contract. Null/CR/LF text is rejected, whitespace is trimmed and case conversion
uses Locale.ROOT. The injected variant validates its result and calls its formatter once.
Empty text is valid. Keep behavior equivalence distinct from evidence about coupling, duplication,
added machinery and whether a concrete variation justifies it.
